description:
Tactical Combat Overhaul
Command your fleet like an RTS, and fight with grounded, tactical rules.

Download (v0.31.2)

Requirements

Starsector 0.98a-RC8
LunaLib (optional, recommended): in-game settings menu
PatchLib (optional, recommended): Allows many improvements to TCO to take place, making everything tidier, uses old fallbacks when PatchLib is not installed

Save compatibility: can be added to an existing save. Removing it from a save it has been used in is not supported.

Features

RTS fleet command
Select ships, give move and attack orders, set formations, stances and control groups, or jump into any ship and fly it yourself.
SpoilerFree camera, box selection, right-click orders, waypoint queues and attack-move
Line, wedge and column formations
Stances: Aggressive, Defensive, Hold Ground, Evasive and Rescue
Command card and ship card for every ship, including allies and visible enemies
Fog of war: you only see what your ships can see

Armor mechanics
Shells penetrate, ricochet off sloped plates, cook off magazines and start fires. Ships burn and break up while their crew escape in pods.
SpoilerKinetic and HE ballistics follow penetration and deflection rules based on the shot and the armor it hits
Magazine cook-offs, wrecked weapons and fires aboard
Death throes: a killed ship drifts and explodes in stages before it goes
Escape pods carrying crew and marines, which your ships can rescue

Ammo, power and logistics
Ballistic guns have limited ammo, ships have reactor power next to flux, and support ships keep the fleet fighting.
SpoilerMagazines and reserves for ballistic weapons, refilled by supply ships and their shuttles
Reactor power drawn by shields and weapons, with meltdowns from deep hits
Repair tenders that send drones to fix engines, weapons and armor mid-battle
Tugs that tow stranded ships to safety
New objectives: the Supply FOB and the Repair Dock

Radar and missiles
Radar finds threats before you can see them; missiles are sorted into radar-guided and heat-seeking.
SpoilerRadar detection by range and radar cross section, with a piloting radar scope
Datalinks that share tracks across the fleet
ECM noise jamming and missile spoofing
IR missiles that can lose cold targets, and flares to decoy them

Boarding
Send marines to capture enemy ships deck by deck.
SpoilerOrders: Standard, Assault, Methodical, Sabotage and Withdraw
Marine experience matters, and survivors gain more
Unknowns aboard: garrison quality, ship layout, the captain, and events during the fight
Marine allocation screen in the campaign to choose who carries how many
Captured ships join your fleet after the battle

Bigger battlefields
Larger maps, with deployment spread out to match.

NPC fleets understand the new mechanics
Enemy and allied fleets get their own supply ships, tenders and TCO hullmods.

Compatibility
Built to work with ship and weapon mods: their weapons, ships and missiles are sorted into TCO's rules automatically and should work with no patches needed.
Almost every system can be tuned or switched off in the LunaLib settings (or in data/config/tco_settings.json without LunaLib).

List of controls
SpoilerTACTICAL COMBAT OVERHAUL 0.30.0 - KEYBINDS
==========================================
Defaults shown. Most keys can be rebound in battle on the Controls (?) sheet, and any of
them can be a side mouse button (MOUSE4 / MOUSE5).

COMBAT - MODES
H ............... pilot the selected ship yourself; H again returns to RTS
T ............... hand the selected ships to the normal ship AI, or take them back

COMBAT - CAMERA (RTS)
W A S D / arrows  move camera (hold Shift for faster)
Middle drag ..... grab and drag the map
Mouse wheel ..... zoom

COMBAT - SELECTING (RTS)
Left click ...... select a ship (allied/enemy ship: show its card)
Left drag ....... box select
Shift + click ... add to / remove from selection
Ctrl + 1-9 ...... save selection as a control group
1-9 ............. select group (twice: jump camera to it)
Shift + 1-9 ..... add group to selection

COMBAT - ORDERS (RTS, right mouse)
Right click ground ........ move
Right click enemy ......... attack
Right click friend ........ escort
Right click stranded friend tow (ship with a tug)
Right click objective ..... capture
Ctrl + right click ........ attack-move (fight anything met on the way)
Shift + right click ....... queue the order after the current one
Right drag ................ move, then face the drag direction
Shift + right drag ........ turn to that facing first, then slide there
Alt + right drag .......... turn in place (or right drag starting on a selected ship)

COMBAT - SHIP COMMANDS (selected ships in RTS)
X ............... stop (also recalls boarding shuttles)
END ............. retreat (any new order calls it off)
F ............... hold fire / open fire
B ............... board the enemy ship under the cursor (Boarding Shuttle Bay)
U ............... keep fighters, shuttles and drones in the hangar / let them out
Y ............... cycle stance (aggressive, defensive, hold ground, evasive, rescue)
L ............... formation: line > wedge > column > break up
C ............... drop flares
N ............... radar off / on
M ............... hold / release radar missiles
O ............... noise jammer: auto > on > off

COMBAT - WHILE PILOTING A SHIP (H)
C / N / M / O ... same as above, for the ship you fly
U ............... hangar hold (H pilot mode only)
K ............... release the radar lock (or right-click the radar scope)
Left click scope  lock a radar contact

CAMPAIGN MAP
F7 .............. marine assignment screen (who gets how many marines for boarding)

Feedback
Bug reports and suggestions are welcome here or on the Discord. For crashes, please attach starsector.log from the starsector-core folder.

Changelog
Spoiler0.31.2
Fixed an issue where captured player ships are refitted by the AI.
Improved transparency on enemy boarding and added a way to get your ships back in battle.
Winning a battle where the other side has captured ships from you and they intend to flee allows you to retake your ships back.

0.31.0
Command ships. Fit a Combat Information Center to a capital (or an Auxiliary CIC to a cruiser) and it becomes
your fleet's eyes: a long-range radar with a sector scan, a built-in ESM suite, faster reports to the rest of the
fleet, sensor picket drones, and a control panel in RTS mode. Lose it, and your fleet loses its picture for a while.
Electronic warfare. Scramble enemy radars, barrage-jam an area, jam incoming radar missiles and disrupt enemy
fire control. All of it runs on reactor power.
The enemy only knows what it has found. The AI no longer sees your whole fleet. It acts on what its ships spot or
track, and sends hunting groups to look for you when it has nothing to fight.
New hullmods. Passive Sensor Suite (ESM), Anti-Radiation Missile Conversion, Tandem Warheads, Militia Lockers,
Expanded Propellant, Blowout Panels, Breaching Charges, Thermal Dispersal Plating, Wet Magazine Stowage, and three
power hullmods.
The Threat boards. Threat ships send waves of their fragments to board you. They're weak and easy to shoot down,
but there are a lot of them, and a ship they take has its whole crew killed and is left drifting.
Missiles hit harder. Every radar missile does 50% more damage and sprint at their target over the last
stretch.
Optional PatchLib support. With PatchLib installed you get fuller fog of war, an AI that understands reactor
power, power stats in the refit screen, and more. Without it old fallbacks are used.

And more, check the changelog on github.

0.30.0
First public release

AI Disclaimer
SpoilerWhile most of the code was written by me, an AI agent helped with workarounds, tidying code and implement certain mechanics.

Credits

Fire effects adapted from GraphicsLib by DarkRevenant (CC BY 4.0)
Thanks to qcwxezda (Unthemed Weapons Collection), whose refit-screen weapon numbers inspired TCO's weapon cards

See CREDITS.txt in the download for details.

discordPostHtml:
A combat overhaul that turns battles into tactical fleet engagements. Command your fleet like an RTS, or jump into any ship and fly it yourself.

Command

  • RTS controls: box select, orders, formations, control groups, attack-move
  • Stances: Aggressive, Defensive, Hold ground, Evasive and Rescue
  • Fog of war, larger battlefields, and two new objectives: the Supply FOB and the Repair Dock

Combat

  • Armor penetration, ricochets, sloped plates, cook-offs and fires
  • Ballistic guns have limited ammo, refilled mid-battle by supply ships
  • Reactor power alongside flux, and meltdowns from deep hits
  • Ships burn and break up while their crew escape in pods

Missiles and sensors

  • Radar missiles need a track to launch; IR missiles chase heat and can be fooled by flares
  • Datalinks, ECM and noise jamming, plus a radar scope when you fly a ship

Boarding

  • Send marines to take ships in deck by deck combat
  • Orders (Assault, Methodical, Sabotage, Withdraw), marine experience, desperate measures taken by defenders.

Logistics

  • Repair tenders, tugs that tow stranded ships, security droids and new hullmods
  • NPC fleets bring their own support ships and use TCO's hullmods too

Built to work with other mods: their ships, weapons and missiles fit TCO's rules automatically.

Requires: Starsector 0.98a-RC8.
Recommended: LunaLib (in-game settings, where every major system can be tuned or turned off) and PatchLib (Several improvements, see the changelog)

Download: https://github.com/reaperyeah420-cpu/Tactical-Combat-Overhaul/releases
Forum post: https://fractalsoftworks.com/forum/index.php?topic=36171.0

Mod thread: https://discord.com/channels/187635036525166592/1561820584726503425 (feedback goes here)

Removing TCO from an ongoing save isn't supported.

DISCLAIMER: While most of the code is made entirely by me, some workarounds and solutions were made using an AI Agent.
aiDescription: Lets you command your fleet like an RTS with box selection, formations, and direct piloting. Introduces realistic armor penetration, magazine cook-offs, and limited ammo for ballistic weapons. Adds support ships like repair tenders and tugs, along with radar systems and boarding mechanics.
